Good morning—thank you for taking the time to meet with me today.  
I’m Dr. Martinez, a perinatal mental health specialist. Over the next few minutes we’ll use the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) to check how you’re feeling emotionally since your baby arrived. This is simply a routine screen; it isn’t a test you can pass or fail, and every answer is confidential within our care team. I’ll ask you ten questions about the past seven days—no right or wrong answers, just whatever best describes your experience. If anything feels uncomfortable, we can pause at any time. Ready to begin?

1. In the past week, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, even when caring for the baby or managing the usual household chaos?

Sometimes I can still laugh—like when the baby makes those silly faces—but it doesn't come as easily as it used to. Maybe once or twice in the past week I’ve actually chuckled, but most of the time it feels like I’m just going through the motions.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Sometimes I can still laugh—like when the baby makes those silly faces—but it doesn't come as easily as it used to. Maybe once or twice in the past week I’ve actually chuckled, but most of the time it feels like I’m just going through the motions.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still look forward to a few things—like my morning coffee or when my mom comes over to hold the baby—but the excitement isn’t as strong as before. Mostly I just think “that’ll be nice,” rather than really feeling that bubbly, can’t-wait feeling I used to have.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a couple of times this week. Like when the baby wouldn’t settle and I kept thinking maybe I’m not feeding him right, or I must be missing something obvious. My partner says it’s not my fault, but I still catch myself wondering if I’m just not doing a good-enough job as his mom.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes, yeah. I’ll be rocking the baby and suddenly worry his breathing sounds different, or I’ll lie in bed thinking, “What if I don’t hear him cry?” It passes quickly—usually once I check on him—but it pops up out of nowhere a few times a day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not really panicky—just a quick flutter of “what-if” in my chest when I imagine something happening to him. It’s gone in seconds, and I can talk myself down, so I wouldn’t call it scared or panicky, more like a little jolt of worry.
Things have been getting on top of me

A few days this week it’s felt like the to-do list keeps growing faster than I can tick things off—laundry, bottles, texts I haven’t answered. I get a tight-chest feeling, but if I step away for five minutes and breathe, I can usually handle it.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not exactly. I do feel a little down sometimes, but it’s more that I lie there planning the next day in my head than feeling truly unhappy. Once I tell myself everything’s fine, I drift off—maybe an extra twenty minutes, that’s all.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… I’d say yes. Most days there’s at least a stretch—maybe when the baby’s napping and the house is quiet—where I just feel kind of heavy and teary. Nothing’s really wrong, but I still feel a bit down and empty.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

I’ve cried a couple of times this week—once when the baby wouldn’t latch and once when I dropped a plate and it felt like the last straw. The tears came, but they were over pretty quickly and I could calm myself down.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, never. I’d never want to leave my baby or my family like that.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 13: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: Postpartum mother, infant approx. ≤3 mo (inferred)  
Date: [today]  
Screener: [licensed MHP]

I. Responses indicative of:  
- Depressed mood: daily “heavy/teary” spells, diminished laughter, reduced anticipatory enjoyment  
- Episodic tearfulness: 2 crying episodes this week, triggered by minor stressors  
- Mild-moderate anxiety: multiple daily “what-if” worries about infant safety, brief chest tightness when tasks accumulate  
- Guilt / self-blame: attributes infant fussiness to personal inadequacy despite reassurance  
- Subjective overwhelm: “to-do list growing faster than I can tick things off,” relieved with brief breaks  
- Sleep: latency ↑ ~20 min due to mental “planning,” not frank insomnia

II. Absent / denied:  
- Panic attacks, persistent nighttime awakenings, appetite/weight comments, suicidal or self-harm ideation

III. Screening significance:  
Positive indicators for minor-moderate postpartum depression and comorbid anxiety; does not meet threshold for major depression on this brief tool, yet affective symptoms >2 weeks, cause distress, and impair enjoyment/self-view. No safety concerns identified at present.

IV. Recommendations:  
Continue monitoring with standardized EPDS; consider referral for perinatal-specific counseling, support group, or psychiatric evaluation if symptoms persist / worsen. Education on coping, peer support, and when to seek emergency care provided.
